title: Become a Greeter - Big Apple Greeter
description: Proud New Yorker? You're already one of us. Join Big Apple Greeter's volunteer family and show visitors the city the way you live it.

blocks.video_label: The Big Apple Greeter apple with a handshake at its heart
blocks.heading: You’re already one of us.
blocks.pitch: The only thing left is making it official.
blocks.cue_label: Scroll to how we do things

blocks.heading: How We Do Things Around Here

items.def: You take up to six guests on an informal, unscripted walk through the streets you know cold. No script, no flag to hold, no memorized dates.
We pair you with visitors based on when you’re free, plus your language, neighborhoods, and interests. Greet once a month or once a week. Family shows up when it can.
The hidden places New Yorkers love and the tourist books miss. You share them like you would with a cousin in town. Yes, even that one.
All five, proudly. The more corners of the city the family covers, the better.
English is all you need. A second language is a superpower here, and a great excuse to use it.
A good walk, new friends from all over the world, and the particular joy of watching someone fall for your city. It makes the world a little smaller and happier.

items.term: Gail’s 22 years at Big Apple Greeter
items.def: Two decades of greets, and a hand in building the international network. This is what staying in the family looks like.
Volunteer Jerry Rumain and his husband visited local Greeters in a Northern Italian village. Cousins abroad, and the door is always open.
One of ours gets shown around by one of theirs. Greeters in more than 130 cities host each other like relatives.

blocks.heading: Not a Walker? There’s Still a Seat at the Table

items.def: Help tell the family’s stories from the lower Manhattan office at 1 Centre Street.
Be our voice with the city. Somebody has to talk to the relatives downtown.
The best job title in the building: pair visitors with the Greeter they were always meant to meet.
Cara Ng, Director of Volunteers & Communications: 212-669-8198 or cara@bigapplegreeter.org

paragraphs.text: Volunteer opportunities are open to everyone without regard to race, ethnicity, color, creed, country of origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability.
New Yorkers with disabilities are warmly welcomed as volunteers, and our office at 1 Centre Street is ADA compliant.

blocks.heading: Join us.
blocks.body: The application takes a few minutes. The stories you’ll tell on your greets took you a lifetime in this city. You’re ready.

blocks.blurb: A free welcome-visitor service from NYC volunteers.
